rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walked every pronoun/demonstrative chunk-by-chunk in order. Chunk2 line16 'it names the thinking...and today you step away' resolves 'it' to the just-named Willison essay in the same sentence; line18 'It isn't' resolves to the un-watched-session comparison in the same sentence; 'its evidence' resolves to the essay named two sentences prior (Why Software Factories Fail). Chunk4 line33 'the exercise's first step' points to the exercise link at line43, but both sit inside the SAME chunk (27-43, one slide), so it is not a forward reference across the cut. Chunk6 'The audit'/'the task'/'pinned commit on a throwaway branch' were all named in chunks 2-3. Chunk7 'the send-off' was named as the chunk-5 header. Chunk9 'You pinned the starting point' calls back to chunk5's send-off beat. No unresolved referent found.

Chunk5 '## Send the task off' (lines 45-51) is the thinnest chunk -- header plus three link titles, no prose -- but the header itself states a claim ('this is where you send the task off') and the three titled links (lecture, exercise, lecture) name what fills that beat, so it does not read as a bare wait-state or context-dependent fragment the way the compendium's example ('let the read finish') does.

Checked all 9 headers against their chunk content: each is a literally true summary (e.g. 'Bring to Module 5' -> content is exactly what to bring; 'Pre-reads before Module 5' -> exactly four optional readings). No header contradicted by its own chunk.

Checked each sub-item across the body: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlatives (no 'one of the most useful' style phrasing); no number-plus-retraction ('one or two candidate tasks' at line31 is a plain count, not a hedge-then-retract); no abstraction-noun stacks (e.g. 'bounded-window reality'); no verb triplets with an empty leg. None of the six sub-patterns found anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: the rule exists to keep bold scarce enough that a bolded span reliably signals a named handle, not editorial emphasis -- diluted, readers stop trusting bold as a wayfinding cue. Line10's whole-sentence bold in Prework is the mandated check_pedagogy.md sec34 task-sizing callout (per the maintainer's own note this run was told to score N/A, not a violation -- confirmed shape matches: bolded floor+ceiling sentence in ## Prework). Lines 22-25's bolded LO verbs (Scope/Walk/Fill/Send off) are one-word handles, one per checklist item, matching the rule's own 'checklist item names' allowed category -- PASS, not flagged. Line31 chunk4 'Start here': grep -n "The question, to you" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/run-the-first-experiment.md -> line31: '**The question, to you:** come with one or two candidate tasks...'. This is a 5-word bolded clause that is not a named law/governor/coined-term/checklist-item -- it functions as a rhetorical address/kicker introducing a prompt, which sec9 lists by name as never-bold ('Kickers/koans/quotes never bold'). The chunk is otherwise unbolded (budget count is within 1-per-slide), so the harm is narrow, but the category match (kicker-shaped address, not a handle) is the actual violation, not the count.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Unbold 'The question, to you:' and let the sentence run as plain narrative, or shrink the bold to a true handle if one is intended.
